Based on the retrieved healthcare Q&A matches, it appears that researchers have found evidence suggesting that patients with fewer than 5 metastatic sites in prostate cancer tend to have better survival rates compared to those with more extensive disease.

The key finding from these studies is that early detection and aggressive treatment of patients with a small number of metastatic lesions may be beneficial for improving long-term survival. This suggests that targeting patients with a limited number of metastatic sites rather than those with many could lead to improved outcomes.

One study found that patients with 5 or more metastatic sites had significantly worse survival rates, while another study noted an inverse relationship between obesity and serum prostate-specific antigen (PSA), suggesting that adjusting PSA levels for body mass index may not be necessary.
